title: The food trail over time: hand-laid, then whatever the ants keep
question: Four seeds of one arm. Does the ant-laid trail read as a trail at all, or as scattered marks that happen to be on the route? And is seed 4 (bottom) the one to aim at, or is a trail that only some colonies hold the wrong target?
context_md:
Answering your question from earlier: *how the hand-laid trail compares to the ant-laid one, and how it changes over time.*

Each panel is one seed. **Time runs DOWN, the route runs ACROSS** — nest at the left, larder at the right. Brightness is channel B. The gutter on the far left is **RED while the hand-laid ramp is still being refreshed** and **GREY after it is withdrawn at frame 6,000**, so the handover is the colour change about a fifth of the way down.

The hand-laid ramp is the clean saturated band at the top of every panel: monotone, full length, nest to larder. What the colony builds instead is the thin blue streaking below it.

**Each panel is on its own scale** so the ant era is legible — the hand-laid band clips to white as a result. Real magnitudes in the meta.

This also corrects something: the harness's `B nest->food` column is a **mean over the whole run**, so it prints a healthy ramp for a run whose route is bare for its last 18,000 frames. It is not evidence the trail survived.

meta.seed 1 ant peak vs hand: 18% -- route BARE in last 6k frames, 0 of 91 cells lit
meta.seed 2: 27% -- 30 of 91 cells lit at the end
meta.seed 4: 78% -- 70 of 91 lit, trail held to the end
